stem: Which technique reduces cost and latency when many requests share a long, identical prompt prefix?

options.text: Prompt or prefix caching offered by the platform, where available
Increasing temperature
Removing the system prompt
Using a smaller font

explanation: Caching a stable prefix avoids reprocessing the same tokens. Availability and pricing differ by provider, so check current documentation.

stem: The model provider has an outage. Which design choice most improves resilience?

options.text: A single provider with no fallback
Timeouts, retries with backoff, a fallback model or provider (or a degraded non-AI path), and clear user messaging
Longer prompts
Caching nothing

explanation: Plan for dependency failure: bound waiting, retry sensibly, provide a fallback, and degrade gracefully instead of failing silently.

stem: Routing simple requests to a small model and hard ones to a larger model is mainly a trade-off between:

options.text: Colour and layout
Cost and latency versus quality, guided by task difficulty and evaluation
Encryption strength
Database size

explanation: Routing exploits the fact that many requests do not need the most capable model. It must be validated by evaluation so quality is not silently lost.

stem: An internal assistant costs far more than forecast. Logs show long conversations resend the entire history every turn, and most questions are simple lookups.
constraints: Quality must not drop for hard questions

options.text: Trim or summarise history, cache stable prefixes where supported, route simple lookups to a cheaper model, and verify on the evaluation set that quality holds.
Reduce the output length limit to the minimum.
Switch all traffic to the cheapest model.
Ask users to ask fewer questions.

rationales.text: Token volume and model choice are the main cost drivers and can be tuned separately.
Cutting outputs alone addresses input token cost.
Evaluation protects quality while optimising cost.
Cheapest model for everything is safe if the bill drops.

explanation: Cost control means reducing tokens, reusing work and matching model to task, validated against quality. Blanket cuts risk quality.
model_answer: Manage context growth, cache stable prefixes, route by difficulty, measure cost per task and quality on the evaluation set, and set budgets and alerts.

stem: A long-running agent processes batches overnight. Occasionally a tool times out and the whole run restarts from scratch, repeating side effects such as emails already sent.
constraints: Some steps are not safe to repeat

options.text: Persist state after each step, make side-effecting steps idempotent or record completion, retry with backoff, and resume from the last checkpoint instead of restarting.
Add a longer timeout and hope failures stop.
Run twice and keep whichever finishes.
Remove the email step.

rationales.text: Checkpointing allows resume without redoing completed work.
Longer timeouts remove the need for state.
Idempotency or completion records prevent duplicate side effects.
Running twice is a safe resilience strategy for side effects.

explanation: Durable execution needs persisted state and safe retries. Idempotency and checkpointing prevent duplicated side effects after partial failure.
model_answer: Store step state, mark completed side effects, use idempotency keys, retry with backoff, and resume from checkpoint; alert when retries are exhausted.
